{{convert|20|°C|°F|abbr=on}}{{Cite journal|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/319524|title=Met Eireann forecasts dry weather for All-Ireland hurling final|first=|last=|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021|journal=Hogan Stand}} | attendance = 82,000 | previous = [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2020]] | next = [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]] }} The '''2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]] on 22 August 2021{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-championship/fixtures|title=GAA Hurling All-Ireland Senior Championship|access-date=20 March 2023|website=GAA}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-2021-roadmap-5403856-Apr2021/|title=GAA unveils 2021 roadmap with leagues starting in May and All-Ireland finals in August|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien|website=The42}} between [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] and [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]], the culmination of the [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. It was the [[List of All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals|134th final]] of that sport's primary competition, the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]. Limerick won the game by 3–32 to 1–22 to claim their third All-Ireland title in four years. This final marked the highest winning score ever achieved in an All-Ireland Senior Hurling final, surpassing Kilkenny's previous record set in the [[2008 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2008]] final.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242236-limerick-crush-cork-to-claim-back-to-back-all-irelands/|title=Limerick crush Cork to claim back-to-back All-Irelands|publisher=[[RTÉ News and Current Affairs]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40364432.html|title=Record-breaking Limerick retain All-Ireland title after powerful win over Cork|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=John|last=Fogarty|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-cork-all-ireland-hurling-final-5529019-Aug2021/|title=Awesome Limerick storm past Cork to retain All-Ireland senior hurling crown|publisher=[[TheJournal.ie#The42.ie|The42.ie]]|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}} The match was also the highest scoring final in the 134-year history of the fixture.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242223-all-ireland-shc-finalcork-v-limerick-updates/|title=Recap: Limerick 3-32 Cork 1-22|date=22 August 2021|work=RTE Sport|accessdate= 25 August 2021}} Due to [[COVID-19]] restrictions, attendance was at 50% (40,000 people).{{Cite web |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0730/1238276-attendance-boost-for-all-ireland-finals-wc-qualifiers/|title=Attendance to increase to 40,000 for All-Ireland finals|first=Damian|last=Lawlor|date=July 30, 2021|via=www.rte.ie}} The match was televised live on [[RTÉ2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]] from the outside studio at Croke Park with analysis by [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]], [[Donal Óg Cusack]] and [[Henry Shefflin]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. The match was also live on [[Sky Sports]], with analysis from [[Jamesie O'Connor]] and [[Ollie Canning]]. ==Background== The two finalists share a [[Cork–Limerick hurling rivalry|Munster rivalry]], with the sides having faced one another more than 100 times in the [[National Hurling League|league]] and championship since their inaugural match in November 1893. The game was the 66th championship meeting between the sides and was their first time meeting in an All-Ireland final. [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] made their 19th All-Ireland final appearance and their third in the last four championship seasons, having missed out in [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-kilkenny-all-ireland-semi-final-report-4742990-Jul2019/|title=Brilliant Kilkenny slay champions Limerick to book first All-Ireland final since 2016|publisher=The 42|date=27 July 2019|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} However, they were undefeated in those recent finals appearances, beating [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2018]] and [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2020]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2020/12/20/talking-points-as-limerick-claim-a-ninth-ever-all-ireland-hurling-title/|title=Talking Points as Limerick claim a ninth ever All-Ireland Hurling Title|publisher=Limerick Post|date=20 December 2020|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} Limerick's seven previous All-Ireland titles were secured at various intervals between [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1897]] and [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1973]]. They were seeking their 10th All-Ireland title overall and their first ever consecutive titles. [[Cork GAA|Cork]] made their 50th All-Ireland final appearance overall and their first since defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2013]]. They last won the title against Galway in [[2005 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2005]], meaning that the 16-year title drought equals their previous record of no titles between [[1903 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1903]] and [[1919 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1919]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/not-since-1903-1919-have-cork-gone-so-long-without-a-hurling-all-ireland-has-their-time-come-again-37162583.html|title=Not since 1903-1919 have Cork gone so long without a hurling All-Ireland, has their time come again?|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 July 2018|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cork-s-near-record-dry-spell-casts-minds-back-to-2004-05-glory-days-1.4351958|title=Cork's near-record dry spell casts minds back to 2004-05 glory days|publisher=Irish Times|date=11 September 2020|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=Seán|last=Moran}} Cork currently lie second only to Kilkenny on the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship records and statistics#General performances|all-time roll of honour]] and were seeking their 31st All-Ireland title, having won all their previous titles at various intervals between [[1890 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1890]] and 2005. For the first time since [[1999 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1999]], not one single member of the Cork team was a holder of an All-Ireland winners' medal. This final was the fourth all-[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] final in the history of the championship, after [[1997 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1997]] between Clare and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]], 2013 between Clare and Cork and 2020 between Limerick and Waterford. It was the eighth time when teams from the same province met.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/the-best-and-worst-hurling-finals-when-teams-from-the-same-province-meet-1.4643227|title=The best and worst: Hurling finals when teams from the same province meet|publisher=Irish Times|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=Seán|last=Moran}} This final marked the third meeting between the teams in the All-Ireland Championship proper. The series currently stood at one apiece, with Cork winning the [[2006 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2006 All-Ireland quarter-final]] and Limerick winning the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2018 All-Ireland semi-final]]. Both sides had already played each other in the 2021 championship, with Limerick beating Cork by 2-22 to 1-17 in the Munster semi-final.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-cork-hurling-2-5483927-Jul2021/|title=First-half goal blast clinches win for Limerick against Cork to book Munster final spot|publisher=The 42|date=3 July [[Sky Sports]] }} ==Pre-match== ===Officials=== On 10 August 2021, the GAA named [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]'s [[Fergal Horgan]] as the referee for the final.{{cite news|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/gaa-confirms-fergal-horgan-to-referee-the-2021-gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-fi/|title=GAA confirms Fergal Horgan to referee the 2021 GAA Hurling All-Ireland Senior Final|publisher=GAA website|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=|newspaper=www.gaa.ie }} Horgan has been an inter-county referee since joining the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] panel of referees in 2011, before joining the national panel in 2012. He officiated three prior matches in the 2021 championship; the Leinster semi-final between [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]], the round 1 qualifier between Wexford and [[Clare GAA|Clare]] and the All-Ireland semi-final between [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and Kilkenny. Horgan also served as referee for the All-Ireland finals in [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2017]] and [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2020]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/fergal-horganselected-to-take-charge-of-his-third-all-ireland-hurling-final-for-cork-and-limerick-showpiece-40736742.html|title=Fergal Horgan selected to take charge of his third All-Ireland hurling final for Cork and Limerick showpiece|publisher=Irish Independent|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} His umpire team was John Ryan ([[Cashel King Cormacs GAA|Cashel King Cormacs]]), Alan Horgan, Mick Butler, and Sean Bradshaw (all [[Knockavilla-Donaskeigh Kickhams GAA|Knockavilla-Donaskeigh Kickhams]]). Wexford's [[James Owens (referee)|James Owens]] was named as the standby referee.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/all-ireland-hurling-final-2021-referee-fergal-horgan-5519517-Aug2021/|title=Tipperary's Fergal Horgan to referee All-Ireland senior hurling final|publisher=The 42|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} The other linesman were Seán Stack ([[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]) and the sideline official, Liam Gordon ([[Galway GAA|Galway]]).{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0810/1240062-horgan-appointed-to-referee-all-ireland-hurling-final/|title=Horgan appointed to referee All-Ireland hurling final|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=10 August 2021|accessdate=11 August 2021|first=|last=}} ===Pageantry=== A number of traditional All-Ireland final elements returned for the first time since the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2019 All-Ireland final]], however, a number of these were scaled back due to [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports in the Republic of Ireland|COVID-19 protocols]]. [[President of Ireland|President]] [[Michael D. Higgins]]’ arrival was announced to the crowd but the custom of him meeting the players along with the [[GAA President]] did not take place. The pre-match parade featuring the [[Artane Band]] made a return.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40362566.html|title=Two cheers for the Rebels: Cork allowed to make second entry onto pitch on Sunday|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021|first=John|last=Fogarty}} [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1996 All-Ireland Championship]] winners [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] were not honoured in the traditional fashion as this year's [[silver jubilee]] team. Instead, [[List of Wexford senior hurling team captains|captain]] [[Martin Storey]] represented the team when he brought out the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] to the plinth on the pitch before the game.{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/319511|title=Martin Storey to represent Wexford's heroes of 1996 as jubilee team at All-Ireland SHC final|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=21 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021|first=|last=}} ==Match== ===Summary=== [[Cian Lynch]] opened the scoring with a point for Limerick in the first minute. [[Gearóid Hegarty]] got the opening goal of the game after two minutes with a low shot after cutting in from the left to make it 1-1 to 0-1. Two minutes later Cork replied with a goal from [[Shane Kingston]] when he cut in from the left and shot high to the net. In the fifteenth minute, [[Aaron Gillane]] scored a second goal for Limerick with a low shot to the right corner of the net after a pass from Seamus Flanagan to make it 2-5 to 1-5.{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/live-blog/30554/12387954/all-ireland-hurling-championship-final-2021-cork-vs-limerick-live|title=All-Ireland Hurling Championship Final 2021: Cork vs Limerick as it happened...|date=22 August 2021|work=SKY Sports|accessdate= 25 August 2021}} Limerick were ahead by 2-8 to 1-6 at the first water break. In the thirty-fifth minute, Gearóid Hegarty got a third goal for Limerick and his second when he ran in on goal and shot low to the left corner of the net. Limerick were ahead by thirteen points at half-time on a 3-18 to 1-11 scoreline. They kept Cork at bay in the second half and scored another fourteen points to eleven for Cork to win the game 3-32 to 1-22 and retain the title.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/northern-ireland/58297943|title=As it happened: Limerick storm to All-Ireland glory|date=22 August 2021|work=BBC Sport|accessdate= 25 August 2021}} ===Details=== {{GAAmatchbox |bg = |date = 22 August 2021 |time= 15:30 |round = All-Ireland Final |report = [https://www.the42.ie/limerick-cork-all-ireland-hurling-final-5529019-Aug2021/ Report] |team1 = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] |score1 = 3-32 {{small|(41)}} |score2 = {{small|(25)}} 1-22 |team2 = [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] |HT = 3-18 {{small|(27)}} - {{small|(14)}} 1-11 |goals1 = G Hegarty 2, A Gillane 1. |points1 = A Gillane 6 (3f), C Lynch 6, P Casey 5, T Morrissey 3, G Hegarty 2, D Byrnes 2 (1f), D Hannon 2, B Nash 1, D O'Donovan 1, S Flanagan 1, G Mulcahy 1, D Reidy 1, P Ryan 1. |goals2 = S Kingston 1. |points2 = P Horgan 12 (10f), S Harnedy 4, N O'Leary 1, M Coleman 1 (f), L Meade 1, J O'Connor 1, S Barrett 1, A Cadogan 1. |location = [[Dublin]] |venue = [[Croke Park]] |attendance = 40,000 |referee = [[Fergal Horgan]] ([[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]) |TV = [[RTÉ]], [[Sky Sports]] }} {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} {{Football kit | pattern_la = _oneillswhite | pattern_b = _vneck | pattern_ra = _oneillswhite | pattern_sh = _oneills20onwhite | pattern_so = _hoops_white | leftarm = 009900 | body = 009900 | rightarm = 009900 | shorts = 009900 | socks = 009900 | title = Limerick }} {{col-2}} {{Football kit | pattern_la = _whitelines | pattern_b = | pattern_ra = _whitelines | pattern_sh = _red_stripes_adidas | pattern_so = | leftarm = ff0000 | body = ff0000 | rightarm = ff0000 | shorts = ffffff | socks = ff0000 |title = Cork }} {{col-end}} {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} {| style="font-size:90%;
